Exact recipe: 473 g semi-coarse wheat flour, 223 g water, 32 g dough butter, 55 g shell-free egg, 56 g sugar, 8 g salt and 10 g dry yeast, two rises, 190 C for 15–18 min, with 48 g butter before and after bake and 9 g sesame topping included. The retained calculation scope incorrectly mentions an egg wash, but rows and recipe agree that the weighed 55 g egg goes in dough and only butter/sesame go on top; no second egg is modeled. Available carbohydrate 45.33 g per bun includes ~38.89 g from refined wheat flour and ~6.22 g sugar. Best independent comparisons: Scazzina et al. 2016 commercial Pagnottelle soft wheat flour roll with sugar (mean GI 62, also reported by study author slide no.22), Kim et al. 2019 (doi:10.1017/S0007114518003446, Tables 1 and 2) soft roll with wheat flour, sugar, milk/fat and yeast (GI 56.2), Wolever et al. 1994 Toronto hamburger bun (mean bread-scale GI 87, glucose-scale ~62 per 2021 supplementary table no. 2212; differing participants and protocol; no double-counting tables as separate studies). The food comparisons translate to comparison-only GK around 28.1 and 25.5. Choice of flour, absence of commercial milk formulation, sugar, butter finish and sesame limit equivalence. Scazzina studied a deliberately high-fibre low-GI sliced bread (41) that would cross the boundary here, but this bun does not replace wheat flour with a fibre-enriched material. No guarantee or lower bound is inferred. No final baked match or numeric approval. Re-review size, recipe, fat finish, sides or process changes.

kevyet-briossisampylat-clever-carrot.reasoning: Directional review for one of nine buns as published, no burger fillings. Exact source uses 405 g strong and 45 g semi-coarse wheat flour with water, milk, yeast, sugar, egg, salt and butter. Two rises; 205 C for 15–20 minutes, optional oven steam, listed egg wash included, no sesame or post-bake butter. Verified available carbohydrate 41.27 g per bun, ~37.0 g from flour, ~3.89 g from sugar. Englyst et al. 2003 primary Table 1 p. 331 pain au lait (GI 63) and bakery brioche (GI 70) support a comparison only; both tested products were richer in fat by available carbohydrate than this lighter recipe. Independent alternatives for a less enriched matrix: Scazzina et al. 2016 soft wheat flour roll with sugar GI 62, Kim et al. 2019 soft wheat roll GI 56.2; their comparison-only GK at this portion is 25.59 and 23.19 respectively. Differences in fat, strong flour, raises and optional steam prevent a point assignment. The 20 boundary would correspond to GI about 48.46; Scazzina's deliberately high-fibre sliced bread GI 41 is a real contrary food design, inapplicable to this recipe's conventional white flour and low fibre. Moderate load cannot be ruled out biologically; likely high is a qualitative judgement for the exact published bare bun. Do not present an interval from comparator points or SEM. Keep the numeric HOLD. Re-review flour, steam, size and serving scope changes.

pohjoisafrikkalainen-msemen-hunajalla-pu.reasoning: Scoped nonnumeric review of current V2 successor, two of four pan-cooked laminated squares with 10 g of the listed serving honey; no other spread/topping. Half-batch inputs: 83.5 g refined wheat flour, 22.5 g durum semolina (including dusting used in lamination), 66.5 g water, 1.5 g salt, 16 g rapeseed oil and 14 g butter. The actual ingredient-based carbohydrate model is verified at 82.99 g/portion; the bread accounts for about 75.76 g, the 10 g honey for about 7.23 g. Published human food comparators for the bread, not its honey topping: Devindra Shakappa et al. (2022), DOI 10.1007/s13197-022-05368-6, Table 2, parota 62.48 (50 g carbohydrate test; glucose reference), a layered pan-cooked wheat flatbread, gives 47.34 comparison-only load applied to the bread's 75.76 g. Shobana et al. (2022), DOI 10.4103/ijmr.IJMR_1935_19, Table 3, methi paratha 60.2 gives 45.61; it contains fenugreek/curd and is only a secondary wheat-flatbread analogy. Vijayakumar et al. Kerala breakfast paper (2017), Table 3, reports a competing lower porotta GI 37.98 (referenced by PMC7791047, row 696), giving 28.77 under the same bread-only check. These are independent comparison points, not a physiological bound or a range for the recipe. The tests do not measure this Moroccan formulation, wheat/semolina proportions, folded oil/butter, cooking method, or honey. A directionally high estimate is supported at exactly two squares with the listed honey. Do not assign a component or whole meal GI number, estimate insulin or response, or transfer the quarantined predecessor's GK100 number. Numeric GK approval and original quarantine stay in place. Re-review ingredient, pan prep, folded fat, honey and serving changes.

karnivore-voilohi-pannulla.reasoning: One of two plain portions of the listed pan-fried skin-on salmon, with all of its allocated cooking fat and butter, without breading, sauce or side. The approximately 0.14 g available carbohydrate contribution recorded here is mainly the butter by recipe composition; label zero does not imply exact laboratory zero. University of Sydney GI research FAQ #11 supports a small expected glycaemic effect of unflavoured fish eaten alone; Holt et al. 1997 (doi 10.1093/ajcn/66.5.1264, Table 3) independently reported a low mean glucose score for its tested fish serving, not a salmon GI and not a serving-ratio proxy. There is no starch, glaze or side within the reviewed mass and preparation. This meets a directional LOW estimate for one plain portion by food-specific evidence plus complete composition. No numeric GI/GK, GK-zero, insulin demand, or individual response is assigned. Re-evaluate coating, sides, portion, product, and retained pan-fat instructions. karnivore-lammaskyljykset-voissa.reasoning: Exactly half of this published batch of unbreaded lamb-and-butter, with all its allocated edible butter, pan fat and resting juices, no side. Salt 2 g per portion, 12.5 g Fineli no. 500 ordinary butter at 0.8 g available carbohydrate per 100 g gives about 0.10 g modeled available carbohydrate per portion. The declared meat composition represents plain lamb. University of Sydney FAQ #11 explains the small expected glycaemic effect of unflavoured meat-only food, and Foster-Powell et al. 2002 (doi 10.1093/ajcn/76.1.5) explains the distinction between absent/untestable GI and small food-group effect for plain meats. Source evidence supports a small directional load for the weighed unsauced portion; this is not a measured lamb or dish GI, GK=0, a claim about all animal-based recipes, or a blood glucose or insulin prediction. indonesialainen-nasi-goreng-aamiaisriisi.reasoning: Exact current V2 is half the pan, including 150 g chilled cooked long-grain white rice, one fried egg and half the sweet soy mixture. Audited 60.95 g available CHO per serving, with rice 52.05 g (AFCD F007661) and brown sugar 7.744 g (AFCD F008969). Wolever et al. 2021, randomized crossover pilot, compared the matching carbohydrate food form including overnight-cooled and stir-fried long-grain polished rice with dextrose. Its primary outcome did not establish a glucose iAUC reduction from cooling or frying and is corroborated by the main fresh-vs-cooled plain-rice trial. The mixed meal of fried fragrant white rice tested by Osman et al. 2017 (https://doi.org/10.1016/j.rsci.2017.06.001, Table 4, n=11) had lower measured GI than the plain rice point estimate, supporting caution about exact meal and rice transfer. The size of the current white rice portion plus sauce sugar and the two in-vivo preparation comparisons support a directional HIGH class. The cultivar, oil type and exact meal matrix differ. No previous recipe or study GI or GK is reused. The existing numerical hold remains active.

rationale.en: The estimate covers one portion with 150 g of long-grain white rice weighed cooked and chilled, one fried egg and the recipe’s sweet soy sauce. The rice and sugar in the sauce provide most of the carbohydrate.

malesialainen-roti-canai-dhalilla-punnit.reasoning: Exact V2 serving is one laminated pan-cooked wheat roti plus half the lentil-coconut dhal, with audited 74.69 g available CHO. The roti includes 62.5 g dry wheat flour and 1.5 g added sugar before cooking (about 47.75 g available CHO together); the dhal includes 50 g dry split red lentils per serving. Robert and Ismail 2012 tested Malaysian flatbread with dhal curry and found similar iAUC to flatbread alone in their study. Tan 2010 primary thesis (https://eprints.ums.edu.my/id/eprint/662/, Table 3.1 and Figure 4.3) independently tested roti canai with dhal and reported mean GI 62.59 at the study test amount. Devindra Shakappa et al. 2022 (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9304465/, Table 2) independently tested wheat parota, another layered pan-cooked refined-wheat flatbread. Taken with the current serving carbohydrates and comparable preparation, the human measurements support directional HIGH for one roti plus this dhal. The recipes, amounts, study cohorts and exact meals differ; none are transferred as GI, GK, numerical bounds or an individual blood-glucose forecast. The numerical hold and the separate old recipe remain unchanged.

rationale.en: The estimate covers one pan-cooked wheat roti and half the recipe’s lentil and coconut dhal. The roti provides most of the carbohydrate, and the lentils in the dhal also contribute.
